title_en: Bank of China, Qinghai Branch v. Liang Guozhi — dispute over repayment of credit card overdraft
keywords_en: civil; credit card dispute; second instance; intermediate people's court; Qinghai Province; natural person; legal person; General Principles of the Civil Law; liability for overdraft after loss reporting; cardholder's liability after credit card robbery; apportionment of liability between merchants and banks; affirmation of original judgment; credit card robbery; oral loss reporting; overdraft consumption; recourse for overdraft amount; robbery; Guo Zhi's dispute over reimbursement of credit card overdraft
full_text_en:
Bank of China Qinghai Branch v. Liang Guozhi — dispute over repayment of credit card overdraft

Plaintiff (Counterclaim Defendant): Bank of China Qinghai Branch.
Legal Representative: Ding Kangnian, President of the Branch.
Agent ad litem: Jiang Yi, Staff Member of the Credit Card Department, Bank of China Qinghai Branch.

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Liang Guozhi, male, 60 years old, retired worker of Qinghai Provincial Highway Bureau, residing in Xining City, Qinghai Province.
Agent ad litem: Zhao Xianhua (wife of Liang Guozhi), retired cadre of Qinghai Metallurgical Metals Import and Export Company.

The plaintiff, Bank of China Qinghai Branch (hereinafter referred to as "Qinghai BOC"), brought an action before the Chengdong District People's Court of Xining, Qinghai Province, against the defendant, Liang Guozhi, concerning a dispute over the repayment of credit card overdrafts. During the proceedings, Liang Guozhi filed a counterclaim.

The plaintiff alleged: The defendant, Liang Guozhi, made overdrafts by using his credit card for consumption. Despite repeated reminders from our staff to repay the amount, he refused to assume the responsibility for repayment. The plaintiff sought a judgment ordering the defendant to repay the overdraft amount and penalty interest totaling RMB 3,331.37.

The defendant argued: Both my wife and I are retired workers and have no need for a credit card. Under pressure from the plaintiff, Qinghai BOC, my wife's employer made her sign the application form to obtain a Great Wall Credit Card; otherwise, she would not have been able to receive her salary. On January 1, 1999, I was robbed by criminals in Qilihe District, Lanzhou City, and my identity card and the supplementary Great Wall Credit Card were stolen. On January 2, my wife made an oral loss report to Qinghai BOC by telephone. All the credit card overdrafts occurred at the Lanzhou Yaiou Shopping Mall after I had left Lanzhou, and were certainly not made by me. After the Great Wall Card was stolen, we immediately reported the loss, but Qinghai BOC did not take the matter seriously, allowing the criminals to continue making purchases until January 5, totaling as many as ten transactions. If Qinghai BOC had performed its duties diligently, the criminals would certainly have been caught when they attempted to make purchases at the Yaiou Shopping Mall. Therefore, the credit card overdraft was the result of Qinghai BOC's dereliction of duty, had nothing to do with me, and I should not bear the responsibility. Furthermore, the usage regulations of the Great Wall Credit Card stipulate that consumption can only be made upon presentation of both the credit card and the holder's valid identification. Despite others using my identity card and credit card to make purchases, the Lanzhou Yaiou Shopping Mall failed to refuse the transactions, and thus bears responsibility. Qinghai BOC should hold the Lanzhou Yaiou Shopping Mall liable for the overdraft. By way of counterclaim, it was alleged that, due to the overdraft following the theft of the Great Wall Credit Card, the plaintiff, Qinghai BOC, deducted money from our credited salary and also caused me to lose three working days accompanying them to Lanzhou to catch the criminals. Qinghai BOC should return the deducted salary and compensate me for my lost working time, totaling RMB 2,590.

The Chengdong District People's Court of Xining, after trial, found the following facts:

On October 27, 1997, Zhao Xianhua, wife of the defendant Liang Guozhi, together with other employees of her former employer, Qinghai Metallurgical Metals Import and Export Company, obtained a Great Wall Credit Card issued by Bank of China through the plaintiff, Qinghai BOC. The primary cardholder was Zhao Xianhua, and the supplementary cardholder was Liang Guozhi. On October 30, 1998, Liang Guozhi further applied for and obtained a supplementary Great Wall Credit Card with the card number 8346990041731017. On January 1, 1999, Liang Guozhi was robbed by criminals in Qilihe District, Lanzhou City, and his identity card and the supplementary Great Wall Credit Card were stolen. On January 2, Zhao Xianhua made an oral loss report to Qinghai BOC, but did not submit a written loss report to the Credit Card Department of the Branch. By January 5, using the stolen credit card and Liang Guozhi's identity card, the criminals had made a total of ten purchases in Lanzhou, resulting in an overdraft of RMB 4,339.75. With respect to this post-loss-report overdraft, Qinghai BOC, in accordance with Article 13 of the "Bank of China Renminbi Great Wall Credit Card Regulations" (hereinafter referred to as the "Credit Card Regulations"), which states: "If a Great Wall Card is lost or stolen, the cardholder shall immediately go to a nearby Bank of China branch or sub-branch to complete the written loss reporting procedures in person, presenting his/her own identity card or other valid identification, and pay the loss reporting handling fee as prescribed. The risk of loss for the lost card occurring before the loss report and within 24 hours after the day of the loss report shall still be borne by the cardholder," voluntarily assumed the overdraft amount of RMB 633 that occurred after 24 hours from the loss report, and deducted RMB 675.79 from the salary credited to the credit card account. Subsequently, Qinghai BOC repeatedly urged Liang Guozhi to repay the overdraft amount and bear the penalty interest of RMB 300.41, but Liang Guozhi refused to repay, on the grounds that the credit card was obtained involuntarily and that the overdrafts were not made by him.

The Chengdong District People's Court of Xining held:

Zhao Xianhua, wife of the defendant Liang Guozhi, signed and obtained the Great Wall Credit Card from the plaintiff, Qinghai BOC, and Liang Guozhi thereby became the holder of the supplementary Great Wall Card. Liang Guozhi not only used the card after obtaining it, but also subsequently applied for another supplementary card. This fact demonstrates that Liang Guozhi's intention to voluntarily hold and use the Great Wall Credit Card was genuine and valid, and the claim that the card was obtained involuntarily cannot stand. The Credit Card Regulations shall be binding on Liang Guozhi's conduct in using the card for consumption.

After the credit card held by the defendant Liang Guozhi was stolen, although an oral loss report was made, a written loss report was not promptly submitted in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Credit Card Regulations. The effective date of the loss report should therefore be calculated from January 4. Although the overdrafts occurring before that date were not made by Liang Guozhi, pursuant to the Credit Card Regulations, he must still bear the risk of such losses. After Liang Guozhi has discharged his liability for the overdraft to Qinghai BOC, if he believes that the liability for the overdraft should be borne by the Lanzhou Yaiou Shopping Mall, he may pursue a claim against the merchant separately. As for the counterclaim raised by Liang Guozhi, it was not supported by evidence and therefore could not be accepted. The claims of Qinghai BOC were well-founded and should be supported in accordance with the law. Accordingly, the Chengdong District People's Court, pursuant to Article 117 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment:

1.  The counterclaim of the defendant Liang Guozhi is dismissed.
2.  The defendant Liang Guozhi shall repay to the plaintiff, Qinghai BOC, the credit card overdraft amount and penalty interest totaling RMB 3,331.37.
The court costs and counterclaim costs totaling RMB 219 shall be borne by the defendant Liang Guozhi.

After the judgment was pronounced, Liang Guozhi, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Xining Intermediate People's Court, Qinghai Province, on the grounds that some facts found in the original judgment were erroneous; that the liability for the overdraft should not be borne by him and the appellee, Qinghai BOC, should exercise its recourse against the merchant; and that Qinghai BOC should return the already deducted overdraft amount and compensate him for the loss of working time incurred while traveling to Lanzhou to catch the criminals.

The appellee, Qinghai BOC, argued in its defense that the original judgment was correct and should be affirmed. The Xining Intermediate People's Court, after trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance and additionally found:

The credit card held by the appellant, Liang Guozhi, was used by others for overdraft consumption in Lanzhou, with the following accounting details: one transaction on January 1, 1999, for RMB 230; four transactions on January 2, for RMB 2,716.75; three transactions on January 3, for RMB 760; one transaction on January 4, for RMB 393; and one transaction on January 5, for RMB 240. The total overdraft amount for these ten transactions was RMB 4,339.75, plus interest and penalty interest on the overdraft of RMB 300.41, aggregating RMB 4,640.16. The appellee, Qinghai BOC, deducted RMB 675.79 from the salary credited to the credit card account, voluntarily assumed the overdraft amount of RMB 633 occurring after 24 hours from the loss report, leaving an actual outstanding overdraft of RMB 3,331.37.

When Zhao Xianhua, wife of the appellant Liang Guozhi, reported the loss to the appellee, Qinghai BOC, on January 2, the bank was on holiday, so an oral loss report was made, and the written loss report was completed on January 4. During the proceedings, both parties acknowledged the loss report date as January 2.

After retirement, the appellant Liang Guozhi contracted a vehicle from Qinghai First Transportation Company to engage in passenger transport. Around January 17, Liang Guozhi received a letter asking him to go to Lanzhou to retrieve a parcel. After reporting this to the appellee, Qinghai BOC, both parties went to Lanzhou together to catch the criminals, but were unsuccessful.

The Xining Intermediate People's Court held:

The loss report date acknowledged by both parties was January 2. Pursuant to Article 13 of the Credit Card Regulations, overdrafts occurring up to and including January 3 shall be borne by the appellant, Liang Guozhi; overdrafts from January 4 onwards shall be borne by the appellee, Qinghai BOC. In this case, there were two overdraft transactions after January 4, totaling RMB 633. Qinghai BOC, in its claim, had already deducted this RMB 633, for which it was responsible, indicating that Qinghai BOC recognized January 2 as the loss report date. After finding this fact that Qinghai BOC had voluntarily assumed the RMB 633, the original judgment's additional finding that the loss report date was January 4 constituted an error in fact finding and should be corrected.

The credit card and identity card of the appellant Liang Guozhi were stolen simultaneously. The criminals' use of these documents to make overdraft purchases infringed upon Liang Guozhi's interests. If Liang Guozhi believes that the Lanzhou Yaiou Shopping Mall bears responsibility for allowing the criminals to make purchases with the card, he should pursue his claim against the Yaiou Shopping Mall separately. This constitutes a separate legal relationship and should not be consolidated with the present case. Liang Guozhi's refusal to assume the responsibility for repaying the overdraft on this ground is untenable.

Due to the overdraft on the credit card held by the appellant Liang Guozhi, the appellee, Qinghai BOC, deducted money from the salary credited to that card account. This was an act to protect its own lawful rights and interests and was not improper. Liang Guozhi's request for the return of the deducted amount is not supported.

After receiving the letter from Lanzhou, the appellant Liang Guozhi reported the matter to the appellee, Qinghai BOC, and both parties went to Lanzhou to catch the criminals. This trip was undertaken to safeguard Liang Guozhi's interests, and the expenses should naturally be borne by Liang Guozhi. Liang Guozhi's appeal request that Qinghai BOC compensate him for the expenses of this trip is not well-founded.

In summary, although the original judgment contained some errors in fact-finding, the final amount awarded was correct and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Xining Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The court costs for the second instance of RMB 113 shall be borne by the appellant Liang Guozhi.
